subtext.text: The speaker device, audio file or if it should be sent as updates.

A .opus or .ogg file is written as Ogg Opus without going through FFmpeg: a single participant is saved as received, more participants are decoded, mixed and re-encoded, which uses more CPU than the other formats.
The video file where to record the camera, or if it should be sent as updates.

When more participants have the camera on, they are composed into an animated grid at the size and frame rate of the video parameters. A .mkv file is written without going through FFmpeg: a single participant is saved as received, more participants are decoded, composed and re-encoded, which uses more CPU. Any other format is composed and encoded by FFmpeg.
The video file where to record the screen sharing, or if it should be sent as updates. It works like the camera, in its own file.
